title: Possible Prophecies About Muhammad
subtitle: A Mosaic comparison worth discussing, and a Paraclete argument that must face the text
summary: The Quran affirms that earlier revelation announced Muhammad. Identifying a particular surviving biblical passage is a separate interpretive claim. Muhammad's likeness to Moses makes Deuteronomy 18 a meaningful comparison, but its Israelite context is a strong objection; John's identification of the Paraclete as the Holy Spirit makes it weaker as an independent prediction of Muhammad. Neither difficulty requires inventing a missing Greek word.

seo.metaTitle: Islamic Prophecies About Muhammad in the Bible | Straight Path
seo.metaDescription: The meaningful Moses–Muhammad comparison, Deuteronomy's context, and why the Paraclete argument cannot rely on an unattested Greek word change.

sections.title: Two Claims That Must Not Be Merged
sections.body:
Quran 7:157 and 61:6 give Muslims a revealed basis for believing Muhammad was announced before his mission. A different question is whether a particular passage in the present Bible independently identifies him.

The first claim depends on the Quran's authority. The second must also answer the earlier text's wording and context. Treating them as identical would make a supposed biblical proof depend on the conclusion it is meant to establish.

sections.title: Why These Two Passages Are Discussed
sections.body:
Deuteronomy 18 speaks of a prophet like Moses; John 14–16 speaks of the coming Paraclete. Muslims have connected both with Muhammad, but their evidential strengths are not equal.

The Mosaic comparison highlights real features of Muhammad's mission. The Paraclete proposal faces an explicit identification within John itself. A sound case for Islam can acknowledge that difference without anxiety.

sections.title: The Positive Mosaic Comparison
sections.body:
Deuteronomy 18:15–19 describes a prophet who receives God's words and delivers what he is commanded. Muhammad resembles Moses as a law-bearing prophet and public leader, whose mission joins worship to communal responsibility. This is a meaningful pattern, not an arbitrary resemblance such as sharing a profession.

The Muslim inference is that Muhammad continues the kind of guidance represented by Moses. The passage does not name him. Whether it predicts him specifically depends on the identity of the promised prophet and the meaning of 'from among their brothers,' not on similarities alone.

sections.title: The Paraclete Is Not a Hidden Translation of Ahmad
sections.body:
Quran 61:6 presents Jesus announcing a messenger named Ahmad. In the surviving Greek Gospel, however, the term is parakletos, an advocate or helper; [John 14:26](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/joh014.htm) identifies the figure as the Holy Spirit.

The proposal that an original periklytos, 'praised,' was changed to parakletos has no demonstrated Greek manuscript support. It should not be repeated as established textual history. A theological belief that Jesus made an announcement is not evidence for an unattested replacement word.

sections.title: The Strongest Objections Are Contextual
sections.body:
Deuteronomy 18:15 speaks of a prophet from among the people addressed. Jewish readers commonly understand Israel's prophetic succession, and Acts 3:22–26 applies the passage to Jesus. These are substantial objections to treating 'brothers' as a clear reference to Ishmaelites.

John's Christian interpretation is stronger still within its own text: the promised figure teaches the disciples and is identified as the Holy Spirit. General traits such as teaching truth fit many figures and cannot override that identification by themselves.

sections.title: What a Word Can—and Cannot—Establish
sections.body:
Kinship language can refer to a related people in some settings, but a word's possible range is not its meaning in every sentence. [The complete Deuteronomy passage](https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Deuteronomy+18%3A15-19&version=WEB%3BISV%3BNIV) must govern the argument.

Likewise, Greek pronouns and grammatical gender do not establish that the Paraclete must be an earthly man. [Christian textual notes](https://bible.usccb.org/bible/john/14) discuss the language in context. A strong identification has to explain the whole passage, including details that do not fit the proposed candidate.

sections.title: How Much Weight Should These Arguments Carry?
sections.body:
For a person who already trusts the Quran, a Mosaic pattern can reinforce the unity of prophetic guidance. For someone asking whether the Quran is true, it is limited supporting material, not an independent demonstration.

A lost or altered announcement is possible within Islamic theology, but it cannot function as a recoverable manuscript proof without evidence. The positive case should therefore rest chiefly on [Muhammad's mission](/articles/who-is-prophet-muhammad) and [the Quran](/articles/why-the-quran), not on reconstructing a text we do not possess.

sections.title: What the Quranic Claim Actually Gives
sections.body:
Quran 7:157 says the messenger is found described in the Torah and Gospel. Quran 61:6 reports Jesus' announcement of Ahmad. Muslims accept these as part of the Quran's account of revelation.

These verses do not quote Deuteronomy 18 or identify John's Greek Paraclete passage by name. Later attempts to locate the announcement should therefore be judged as interpretations, not protected as if the Quran had supplied their full argument.

sections.title: Respect the Earlier Reader's Reasoning
sections.body:
Acts 3 gives an explicit Christian application to Jesus. John 14:26 gives an explicit identification with the Spirit. A Christian who reads them that way is following primary texts, not merely ignoring an obvious Muslim proof.

A Muslim can dispute those texts' final theological authority while representing them accurately. The disagreement then becomes the real one: whether the Quran is God's corrective revelation and whether Muhammad is His messenger.

sections.title: A Better Conversation About Prophecy
sections.body:
Discuss Muhammad's likeness to Moses as a serious pattern, acknowledge why Deuteronomy's original setting favors an Israelite reference, and retire the unsupported Greek substitution argument.

Then turn to [Who Is Prophet Muhammad?](/articles/who-is-prophet-muhammad). A person can reach a reasoned Islamic conclusion without claiming that a Christian must see Muhammad named unambiguously in the present Gospel.

quranVerses.translation: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered prophet, whom they find written in what they have of the Torah and the Gospel, who enjoins upon them what is right and forbids them what is wrong and makes lawful for them the good things and prohibits for them the evil and relieves them of their burden and the shackles which were upon them. So they who have believed in him, honored him, supported him and followed the light which was sent down with him - it is those who will be the successful.

quranVerses.translation: And [mention] when Jesus, the son of Mary, said, "O children of Israel, indeed I am the messenger of Allah to you confirming what came before me of the Torah and bringing good tidings of a messenger to come after me, whose name is Ahmad." But when he came to them with clear evidences, they said, "This is obvious magic."

This is according to all that you desired of Yahweh your God in Horeb in the day of the assembly, saying, “Let me not hear again Yahweh my God’s voice, neither let me see this great fire any more, that I not die.” Yahweh said to me, “They have well said that which they have spoken. It shall happen, that whoever will not listen to my words which he shall speak in my name, I will require it of him.
But the Counselor, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things, and will remind you of all that I said to you.

Now when the day of Pentecost had come, they were all with one accord in one place. Suddenly there came from the sky a sound like the rushing of a mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting. Tongues like fire appeared and were distributed to them, and one sat on each of them. They were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and began to speak with other languages, as the Spirit gave them the ability to speak.

faq.question: Does Deuteronomy 18 name Muhammad?
faq.answer: No. Muslims point to a meaningful likeness to Moses, but the passage's Israelite setting and Christian application to Jesus are substantial alternative readings.

faq.question: Does Paraclete mean Ahmad?
faq.answer: No. The surviving Greek reads parakletos, an advocate or helper, and John 14:26 identifies the figure as the Holy Spirit. The proposed periklytos substitution lacks demonstrated manuscript support.

faq.question: Does this disprove Quran 61:6?
faq.answer: It limits a proposed identification of the announcement, not the whole question of whether Jesus announced a later messenger. The Quran's authority must be judged through its broader evidence.

faq.question: Can a missing original passage prove the case independently?
faq.answer: Not without evidence of that wording. A theological explanation of why texts differ is not the same as a surviving textual proof.

faq.question: How should this be used in dawah?
faq.answer: Present the Mosaic comparison honestly, state the contextual objections, and keep the main argument grounded in the Quran and Muhammad rather than in an unsupported word change.
